submitter: framework_prompts_positive_voice lane (migration 641 redraft, round 2 - resubmission of corr 6c92d154 after an OWNER-directed change to the approved text)
rationale:
Migration 641 was APPROVED at round 1 (corr 6c92d154) and rehearsed twice under ROLLBACK, but its gate 2 - the owner's read of the exact inserted block - had not happened when he changed the text. On 2026-09-03 he read four candidate blocks BLIND (letters randomised, key sealed in the lane NOTES before presentation, the approved text included as an unlabelled control). He leaned to the control for its warmth, was then shown what its opening frame does to real data, and directed: drop the frame, keep the rest, and author subjects as fuller sentences or phrases.

The frame is the whole change. The approved text opened "You'll want to know {{.current_section.subject}}. That's what this section is for." - a fixed sentence with a hole, so the subject must be a short lower-case sentence fragment or the sentence breaks. That constraint is unenforceable: subjects come from two producers, one of them the build-site-planner writing unattended. Measured on the render harness against REAL orchestration_states rows, the frame renders broken on both live shapes (see grounded_in). The redraft prints the subject verbatim on its own line and leaves the sibling list byte-identical to the approved text.

This is a REGISTER change in service of the owner's 2026-09-02 positive-prompting directive, and it REMOVES a coupling rather than adding one: with no frame, every subject shape renders grammatically, so the previously-open tier-1 planner question stops being a correctness matter. What it does NOT change: the delta is still two changes in one transaction (block + sections_for_render appended to input_fields), and every guard the round-1 council asked for is byte-for-byte as approved.

The live page-content-writer prompt_template moved from 14,111 to 14,621 chars and from 9 to 10 em dashes during this session (another lane's edit to the same row), which is why the census asserts pre/post EQUALITY rather than a literal - a literal census would have failed this apply.

risks:
1. The owner's read of these exact bytes (gate 2) is NOT yet done; this submission is the review of the change, not the approval of the words. Nothing applies before his read is recorded in the apis.uk lane's NOTES.
2. The subject now prints verbatim into the writer's prompt in page voice, so it will tend to be reproduced closely in the section's opening line. Under this decision that is the INTENT, not leakage, but it moves authorship of a page's first line into the subject data, which two lanes author. A phrasing spec is owed to both before either writes data; until it lands, the stale 'must complete "You'll want to know ___"' rule in the 443 lane's CONTRIB must not be followed.
3. The build-site-planner still writes capitalised noun phrases containing em dashes, which now print verbatim as a section's opening line. Not a correctness failure any more, but a register one; it is owed as a separate migration on the apis.uk lane's rule-17 anchor, and their migration 729 pins the same anchor and is blocked on an owner permission decision, so it re-anchors on top rather than the reverse.
4. Two copies of the text in one file remain a standing hazard for any future edit; the decode-and-compare check is recorded in the lane RUNBOOK, including that its first version false-alarmed on a trailing newline.
